question.worked_solution:
First, let's factor the expression as a perfect square trinomial in ${p}^{2}.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}16{p}^{4}+72{p}^{2}+81 & ={(4{p}^{2})}^{2}+2\cdot (4{p}^{2})\cdot 9+{9}^{2} \\  & ={(4{p}^{2}+9)}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to factor the sum of squares in the parentheses. To do this, we first write it as a difference. Then, we rewrite the second term using ${i}^{2}=-1.$ Finally, we factor as a difference of squares.

$$
\begin{aligned}4{p}^{2}+9 & =4{p}^{2}-(-9) \\  & =4{p}^{2}-9({i}^{2}) \\  & ={(2p)}^{2}-{(3i)}^{2} \\  & =(2p+3i)(2p-3i)\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting this back into our main expression, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}16{p}^{4}+72{p}^{2}+81 & ={(4{p}^{2}+9)}^{2} \\  & ={((2p+3i)(2p-3i))}^{2} \\  & ={(2p+3i)}^{2}{(2p-3i)}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
